The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the RMS Titanic.

To understand blockchain technology, imagine a massive, shared notebook that is kept by thousands of people all over the world. In a traditional system, like a bank, one central authority holds the only copy of the ledger and records every transaction. If that central record is lost, altered, or hacked, the data is compromised.

In a blockchain system, instead of one notebook, everyone has their own identical copy. When a new transaction occurs, it’s like writing a new page in everyone’s notebook at the same time. Before the page is accepted, the group must verify that the entry is valid and matches what they already have. Once agreed upon, the page is sealed and added to the chain. Because everyone has a copy, no single person can secretly change a past entry without everyone else noticing and rejecting the change. This makes the record extremely secure, transparent, and trustworthy, as it relies on collective agreement rather than a single point of control.
